---
title: Getting started
description: Install HTSeqCountCluster and prepare an explicit sample manifest.
---

HTSeqCountCluster submits one `htseq-count` task per BAM file to Slurm or
PBS/Torque. Version 2.0 requires Python 3.10 or newer and HTSeq 2.1 or newer.

## Project origin

This project grew from an [issue I opened on the HTSeq
repository](https://github.com/simon-anders/htseq/issues/43) about using multiple
cores to process many BAM files. That discussion inspired this approach: run one
`htseq-count` job per sample in parallel, then merge the count tables.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install HTSeqCountCluster
```

The batch environment must provide `htseq-count` and HTSeqCountCluster;
environment-module configuration remains site-specific.

## Prepare a sample manifest

Create a two-column CSV file:

```csv
sample_id,bam_path
control-1,/data/rnaseq/control-1.bam
treated-1,alignments/treated-1.bam
```

Relative BAM paths resolve from the manifest directory. Sample identifiers must
be unique and cannot contain directory separators. Each task writes
`<sample_id>.counts.tsv` to the output directory.

## Preview before submitting

Dry runs validate the manifest, BAM files, and annotation and write scheduler
scripts without calling `sbatch` or `qsub`:

```bash
htseq-count-cluster run \
  --scheduler slurm \
  --dry-run \
  --infile samples.csv \
  --gtf genes.gtf \
  --outpath counts
```

Submission metadata remains under
`counts/.htseq-count-cluster/<submission-name>/` for provenance and diagnosis.
